messages.subject: 3D to 2D plot?
parts:
Hi Phil,

 

Using lavaan I have found that model fit for a unidimensional graded response model is good when I add a covariance between residuals of two items. For example, I have specified the model in mirt like this:

 

model <- "

F1 = 1-8

R25 = 2,5

CONSTRAIN = (a2, 2,5)"

mod <- mirt(data, itemtype = "graded", model, SE=TRUE, verbose=FALSE)

 

In which I have added the covariance between residuals of items 2 and 5.

 

I want to make a test-information plot for combined items in this model (e.g., items 1-5 for plot 1, items 6-8 for plot 2), but because I need to add the covariance as a new factor, this plot is a 3D-plot. Is there any way to visualize this as a 2D-plot, as the second factor is not really informative in this case? I also prefer to have a 2D-plot because it is easier to understand for people who will read my paper.

 

Or is there maybe another way to specify this model in a way that I will get a 2D-plot?

 

Thank you!

Iris

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: 3D to 2D plot?
parts:
I don't think this is possible. Because there is a residual correlation effect looking at just one trait in isolation is no longer kosher, for the composite. You can look at 2D slices for items though, at least for some of them, but for the global information I don't see a great way around this. 

Phil
